title: FPS2's eleven arms again on a freshly started DF (FPS2 ran on a two-day-old process that ran BOATS several times slower), read by the harness's stopwatch (two 4-s windows, tick counter stamped unpaused at each end) at every 2,000-tick sample, so the step verb's ~5 s per call stays out of the rate; 25,000 ticks per replicate. What load makes a fort slow? Ticks per wall second at the graphics cap 60, tick cap 1000, tool on, as each factor is scaled on BOATS (the user's 6x6 Boatsbowed copy, 29 citizens, 90 wild): wild land animals +200/+500 (cx-load wild, the tool's place), citizens +30/+60 (created dwarves made citizens by makeown, a working citizen's labors), caverns breached 1/3 (a stair shaft from the surface to each band's floor, the caves marked discovered), all three at once; and embark size 2x2/4x4/6x6 on fresh 7-dwarf embarks at CTRL's tile (region4 29,20). Throughput is the harness's ticks / wall seconds per 1,000-tick step, first step discarded.
fork: Which of wild animals, citizens, open caverns and map size costs a fort its speed, and how much per unit, so the user's ~30 FPS can be placed on the curve.

predictions.expects: t/s falls with citizens and wild units; citizens cost more each (jobs, needs)
cav3 slower than base once dwarves and creatures use the shaft; little in 6,000 ticks if nobody walks it
e6 slower than e4 slower than e2 at equal citizens

predictions.model: the heavy fort approaches the user's 30
predictions.expects: H_heavy well under A_boats; 30 t/s would need more than +500 wild/+60 citizens

kill_criterion: a replicate whose lever receipt shows fewer than 90% of the asked units placed, or a breach whose walk line reads false at the second sample, did not test its factor
culling: the first sample of every replicate (warm-up, load-time caches)
